questions.question: Ground-up losses are observed only when $X>d$, for a fixed threshold $d$. What happens to a loss exactly equal to $d$ in this left-truncated dataset?
options: It does not enter the dataset.
It enters with recorded value zero.
It enters only if its density is positive.

questions.question: Loss $X$ has density $f_\theta$ and entry probability $p_\theta=\mathbb{P}_\theta(X>d)>0$. For an exact selected value $x>d$, which contribution is correct for every such model?

Only losses $X>d$ are recorded, but the dataset stores insurer excesses $y=X-d$. Let $f_\theta$ be the ground-up density and $p_\theta=\mathbb{P}_\theta(X>d)>0$. Which contribution is valid for every such model at reported $y>0$?

An analyst receives exactly $n\ge1$ independently selected losses above threshold $d$ and no information about how many losses were excluded. Does the conditional sample size alone determine the population fraction exceeding $d$?
options: Yes; a known threshold determines that fraction without a loss model.
Yes; exclusion probability can be read from the sample minimum.
No; the unobserved population count is unspecified.

questions.question: Losses enter a dataset only when $X>d$. For a candidate parameter $\theta$, the model gives $\mathbb{P}_\theta(X>d)=0$, yet a selected value $x>d$ was observed. How should that candidate be treated?
options: It is incompatible with the observed selection.
It receives an infinite conditional likelihood.
It requires replacing the denominator by one.
It remains admissible because every exact continuous point has probability zero.

questions.question: Ground-up loss density is $f_\lambda(x)=\lambda \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda x}$ for $x>0$, with rate $\lambda>0$. Losses enter only above $d=10$. Which conditional density expression for exact loss $x=14$ is valid for every $\lambda>0$?
Loss density is $f(x)=1/100$ for $0<x<100$ and zero elsewhere. Only losses above 60 are selected. Using this version, what is the conditional density at selected loss 80?
Loss $X$ is 0, 5 or 10 with probabilities 0.4, 0.2 and 0.4. Only losses $X>5$ are recorded. What probability does the selected loss distribution assign to value 10?

There are $n=3$ independent exact selected losses $x_i>d$. Their ground-up log densities sum to $A(\theta)$ and their common entry probability is $p_\theta>0$. Which conditional log-likelihood formula is valid for every such model?
A continuous loss has density $f(x)=0.1$ throughout $(10,10.1)$ and entry probability $\mathbb{P}(X>10)=0.02$. Only losses above 10 enter the dataset. What is $\mathbb{P}(10<X<10.1\mid X>10)$?

Loss $X$ has density $f_\theta$ and CDF $F_\theta$. Exact observations are selected only from $(a,b]$, where $a<b$ and $F_\theta(b)>F_\theta(a)$. Which selection probability normalises their conditional density for every such model?

For fixed $n\ge1$, a selected log-likelihood is $\sum_i\log f_\theta(x_i)-n\log p_\theta$, with ground-up density $f_\theta$ and positive entry probability $p_\theta$. Which condition guarantees that dropping the normalisation leaves maximising parameters unchanged for every such model and dataset?
options: When entry probability is constant in the parameter.
Whenever the threshold is numerically known.
Whenever every observed loss exceeds the threshold.
Whenever sample size is treated as fixed.

questions.question: Each selected loss has marginal density $f_\theta(x)/p_\theta$ above threshold $d$, but selected records may be dependent. What additional information is needed to justify multiplying these marginal contributions?
options: That every recorded loss is observed exactly rather than censored.
That the records are independent, or their joint law factorises.
That all records share the same truncation threshold $d$.
That each record has a positive entry probability $p_\theta$.

questions.question: Independent exponential losses of rate $\lambda>0$ are recorded only above 100. The exact ground-up observations are 120 and 150. What conditional maximum likelihood estimate of the rate follows?

Independent continuous losses share density $f_\theta$. Record 1 is selected above $d_1$, and record 2 above $d_2$. Their distinct entry probabilities are $0<p_1\ne p_2<1$. Which formula gives the selected exact-data likelihood for all $x_1>d_1,x_2>d_2$ with positive density?

For one exact selected loss $x>d$, candidate models A and B have entry probabilities 0.1 and 0.5. Their supplied ground-up density values at x are 0.02 and 0.03, respectively. What is the ratio $L_A/L_B$ of their conditional selected-data likelihoods?

For each $\theta>b>0$, ground-up loss is uniform on $(0,\theta)$. Only exact losses in a fixed interval $(a,b]$, with $0<a<b$, are selected and sample size is fixed. Can those selected amounts identify $\theta$?
options: Yes; their density remains $1/\theta$ after selection.
Yes; the selected maximum must equal $\theta$.
No; their conditional law is uniform on the same fixed interval.
Yes; every possible value of $\theta$ has the same population mean.

questions.question: An exact continuous loss $x>d$ is fitted with density family $f_\theta$ after left truncation, with positive entry probability for each candidate. An analyst changes each density only at the observed point $x$ to favour one parameter. Does this create new distributional evidence for that parameter?
options: Yes; the new density height creates positive mass at $x$.
Yes; a changed density value changes the entry probability.
No; conditional likelihood values can never depend on density versions.
No; isolated density changes leave observation laws unchanged.

questions.question: Use the density version $f_\theta(x)=1/\theta$ for $0<x\le\theta$, zero elsewhere. Losses are selected above known $d=10$ and exact selected data are 12 and 18. The parameter satisfies $\theta>10$. Which conditional MLE respects the support?

Exactly $m$ independent population losses were sampled; $0<n<m$ exceeded $d$ and exact selected values $x_i$ are known. Let $0<p_\theta=\mathbb{P}_\theta(X>d)<1$ and density $f_\theta$. Omitting only the combinatorial count factor, which joint likelihood expression is valid for every such model?
